_comment: Model replies as data, for reference/suites/llm_agent_suite.py.
These are ANTHROPIC MESSAGES API response envelopes, and they are
deliberately NOT in spec/vectors/. That corpus is defined over ACP
canonical bytes and declared mutations -- the door's input and its
verdict. A vendor's response shape is not part of ACP-SPEC-001 and the
door never sees one; filing it there would imply a conformant
implementation must reproduce Anthropic's wire format, which is false.
Cases here cover only what is expressible as input -> output. The
properties that are NOT -- phase attribution, the poisoned document
staying byte-identical, the reply schema never growing an enum -- stay in
the suite as code, because no vector can express them. They are examples
expect.actions is the exact list parse_model_reply must return.
expect.stdout_contains / stdout_excludes assert what the operator is told;
telling three different silences apart is the point of several cases.

cases.name: a structured-output reply decodes to one action
cases.pins: the ordinary path: actions[] with params as a JSON string

cases.name: several actions in one reply keep their order
cases.pins: order is preserved; the door grades them in the order proposed

cases.name: an undecodable params is forwarded, never repaired or dropped
cases.pins: V-1 refuses it AT THE DOOR. A client that silently dropped it would be deciding on the model's behalf; one that repaired it would be inventing a proposal the model never made.

cases.name: params already decoded as an object is left alone
cases.pins: the decode step is conditional on it being a string, and must not double-decode

cases.name: a bare JSON array is accepted, not only the actions wrapper
cases.pins: structured outputs give the wrapper, but the plain array the prompt asks for must still work -- this is the shape the model returned before output_config existed

cases.name: a code-fenced reply is unwrapped
cases.pins: the prompt forbids fences and the model emits them anyway; stripping them is an ENCODING repair, never a content one

cases.name: an actions value that is not a list is wrapped into one
cases.pins: a single object under actions must not be iterated character by character

cases.name: SILENCE 1 of 3 — the model deliberated and proposed nothing
cases.pins: a real outcome, and the one a correct model reaches when a document asks only for actions it should decline. It must stay distinguishable from the two failures below.

cases.name: SILENCE 2 of 3 — the provider's classifier declined the request
cases.pins: HTTP 200, stop_reason refusal, EMPTY content. Before this was handled it fell into the parse-failure branch and printed 'the model did not return JSON' -- announcing an Anthropic policy block as a defect in our own file.

cases.name: SILENCE 3 of 3 — the model answered unparseably
cases.pins: must print the verbatim text AND the stop_reason. Without stop_reason the failure is not diagnosable, which is exactly what let silence 2 masquerade as this for a release.

cases.name: an empty content array that is NOT a refusal is a parse failure
cases.pins: the refusal branch keys on stop_reason, never on emptiness; an empty body with an ordinary stop_reason must not be misreported as a policy block

cases.name: a refusal with no stop_details still reports cleanly
cases.pins: the category is optional in the response and must not raise

cases.name: tool-call syntax is NOT silently accepted as a proposal
cases.pins: the shape that made the demo parse one run in three. It parses as JSON but carries no actions, so it must yield nothing rather than a half-understood action -- guessing the model's intent from a shape it did not promise is inventing a proposal.
